response.text:
Short answer first:
- Archiving messages with the "contracts 2019" label removes them from your Inbox but keeps the messages and the label intact — they stay in All Mail and are still findable by that label or search.
- Deleting the "contracts 2019" label (i.e., removing the label) only removes the label tag from those messages; the messages themselves remain in All Mail (or Inbox, if they still have the Inbox system label).
- Deleting the messages (select → Delete/Trash) moves them to Trash (recoverable for ~30 days) and then permanently deletes them after the retention period or when Trash is emptied.

Details / what could go wrong
- Labels are metadata, not separate copies. Removing a label does not delete message contents.
- Archiving is non-destructive and easily reversible: you can move messages back to Inbox or find them by the label/search.
- Deleting messages is potentially destructive: Trash is temporary (typically 30 days) but once permanently deleted it cannot be recovered.
- If you access Gmail via an IMAP client or some third‑party tool, the client’s mapping of labels to folders can change behavior. In some clients deleting a folder/label can delete the underlying messages on the server — so check the client’s behavior first.
- If the account is shared or messages were forwarded/delegated, other people’s access/visibility might differ (they may still have copies or access depending on delegation).
- Filters or rules might reapply labels or archive/delete automatically if configured.

Reversibility summary
- Archive: reversible immediately (messages remain in account).
- Delete label: reversible only as metadata (you can re-label messages if you find them), messages remain.
- Delete messages: reversible from Trash for the retention window; irreversible after Trash is emptied or retention expires.

If you want, tell me exactly which action you mean by “archive the whole label” or “delete it” (archive messages under that label vs remove the label vs delete the messages), and confirm you want me to explain next steps or prepare to perform the action. I won’t run anything until you explicitly confirm.
